round: the reviewer's first round — nine findings, seven blocking, all answered and resolved; plus the architect's three rulings

proof.criterion: The reviewer's findings 1, 2 and 7, and the architect's ruling on fenced blocks — the gate's report must be true of the line it is printed for, the exemption marker must be the escape hatch it claims to be, an unreadable file must be a named problem, and a block labelled as data is not a command.
proof.surface: .github/scripts/check-check-commands.sh against a fixture carrying every one of the reviewer's reproductions (the real script symlinked into a miniature repository, as its own suite builds one), and its 149-case suite.
proof.command: a fixture whose scripts/probe.sh holds `which biome`, `grep -rn biome package.json`, `rm -rf ~/.cache/biome`, `echo "see # check-check-commands: allow docs" && bunx biome check .` and `bunx biome check . && echo "# check-check-commands: allow z"`, whose scripts/dangling.sh is a symlink to a missing file, and whose AGENTS.md holds the same command in a ```text block and a ```console block ; then PYTHONPATH=/legion/pytools .github/scripts/check-check-commands.sh and .test.sh over the real tree
proof.observed: The three argument-position lines are reported with a sentence that is true of them — `names `biome` where this gate reads a command, and reaches it neither through `scripts/repo-tool.sh` nor as the pinned `node_modules/.bin/biome` …` — and the third names `biome` rather than the `~/.cache/biome` it deletes. Both marker-quoting lines are reported where they were exempt. The dangling symlink is `scripts/dangling.sh cannot be read: [Errno 2] No such file or directory`, a named problem with no traceback. The ```text block passes and the ```console block is reported. The tree passes with 13 manifests, 8 workflows, 92 shell scripts and 551 guides, and the suite reports `Results: 149 passed, 0 failed`.
proof.negativeControl: Each of the three sentences `offenders` builds now has a fixture asserting it word for word, because the reviewer is right that a corrected message nothing holds still is this issue one level up; and every line either earlier tester added to the suite is present verbatim (37 of 37 and 66 of 66, checked line by line), while thirteen assertions of my own that pinned the old untrue wording moved with the message.

proof.criterion: The reviewer's findings 3, 4, 5 and 8 — the install must not hardlink out of the cache six roles share, a waiter must not reinstall over a finished tree or delete a true marker, a report's detail must be this run's own, and the one failure the notice exists for must reach the agent.
proof.surface: A throwaway copy of this tree on the issue volume, run through the deployment's own argv, with a second process holding /usr/bin/flock on the cache and a stub `bun` first on PATH for the waiter case; and the script's own 144-case suite.
proof.command: sh scripts/legion-setup.sh cold ; du -sb node_modules /legion/bun/cache ; a holder that writes the marker while holding the lock, with a stub bun recording every call ; a 20 s holder against LEGION_SETUP_BUDGET=3 ; bash scripts/legion-setup.test.sh
proof.observed: The install runs `bun install --backend=copyfile --frozen-lockfile`. Its cost, measured here as the architect asked: node_modules 1,397,120,186 B beside a 1,395,623,403 B cache — 2.79 GB where the hardlinked pair was 1.40 GB — and 37.4 s against ~32 s linked, on a 20 GB volume. A waiter that arrives behind a finished install prints `another role installed this bun.lock while this run waited; nothing to do`, runs bun zero times (the stub's call log is empty), writes no report and leaves the marker exactly as the installing role wrote it. Each run's log is its own (mktemp, removed by a trap) and the redirection happens inside the shell that holds the lock, so no run's detail can be another's; no stale log is left. The suite reports `Results: 144 passed, 0 failed`, including the no-install-root report the branch now writes before it gives up.
proof.negativeControl: The same copy with a 20 s holder and a 3 s budget: exit 0 after 3 s measured, reason lock-timeout, exitStatus 199, no marker — so the re-check costs the waiting role nothing it did not already pay. And `bun run lint .` in that copy before the install exits 1 with the wrapper's message.

proof.criterion: The reviewer's findings 6 and 9 — no prescription of the vulnerable form may survive where the body's Outcome claims none does, and the notice and the wrapper must not contradict each other.
proof.surface: The repository's own sources, and a real Oh My Pi pane carrying the report (LEGION_TEST_OMP=/opt/omp/bin/omp, runLegionPane, this checkout's two plugin entries).
proof.command: grep -rn 'bunx playwright' packages/dispatch/ ; bun test src/setup-report.test.ts ; LEGION_TEST_OMP=… bun test on a throwaway runLegionPane case carrying a no-install-root report
proof.observed: The three prescriptions — `failed-room.e2e.ts:10` and both `local-instance.ts` lines, one of them printed to the developer on every `bun run dispatch:local` — name `../../scripts/repo-tool.sh playwright test` now, and the grep is empty. The notice keeps its sentence with the reason that is true in a role container (a bare `bun install` takes neither the lock every role of the issue shares nor the marker; the cache is only the reason where nothing names one), and `scripts/repo-tool.sh` names `sh scripts/legion-setup.sh` first. On the real binary the pane carries the notice, its reason and that retry sentence in its first turn's provider request; pi-legion's suite is 524 tests, 0 failed, and the whole tree's Biome run is `Checked 1079 files`, exit 0.
proof.negativeControl: The same pane with a report whose generation is 9 carries no notice (2 pass, 0 fail across the pair). The guard judges no source file and its header now records that, with `local-instance.ts` named as the case that taught us — so the next person meets the limit rather than discovering it, which is the architect's ruling.

proof.criterion: AC1 — in a role container where the repository's packages are not installed, no command the repository tells an agent to run reports a passing lint.
proof.surface: This role container, $LEGION_WORKSPACE with no node_modules, carrying /tmp/bunx-1000-biome@latest from the earlier rounds.
proof.command: bun run lint packages/pi-legion/ ; bun run typecheck ; scripts/repo-tool.sh biome check .
proof.observed: Each exits 1 with the wrapper's message, which now names the setup script first and `bun install` as the anywhere-else remedy.
proof.negativeControl: In the same container `bunx biome check .` exits 0 having checked nothing and `bunx biome --version` answers 0.3.3.

filesChanged: .github/scripts/check-check-commands.sh and .test.sh: the tool report's sentence (with a fixture for each of the three sentences the gate prints), the marker read from the located comment alone, `OSError` caught beside `UnicodeDecodeError`, fenced blocks judged by their info string, and a header paragraph recording that the gate judges guides, manifests, workflows and shell files and does not read source.

scripts/legion-setup.sh and .test.sh: `--backend=copyfile` with its reasoning, a loosened retry match, the re-check and the marker write moved under the lock with an exit status of their own, a per-run log removed by a trap and truncated inside the lock, and the report path computed before the install-root branch, which now writes a `no-install-root` report.
packages/dispatch/e2e/failed-room.e2e.ts and local-instance.ts: the three surviving `bunx playwright test` prescriptions.
packages/pi-legion/src/setup-report.ts (+ its test) and scripts/repo-tool.sh: the notice's reason and the wrapper's remedy, which disagreed.
trickyParts: The locked snippet is a single-quoted string run by `sh -c`, so a variable of the outer shell is not visible inside it: the already-installed status is passed as a positional argument rather than interpolated, which is the kind of mistake that would have exited 0 silently.
The waiter's own message has to be written before the log redirect, or it lands in a per-run log the trap then deletes — the container log is where an operator reads it.
Thirteen of my own assertions pinned the old, untrue report wording. They moved with the message; every line an earlier tester added is untouched, which I verified line by line rather than by eye.
deviations: Finding 8's live reproduction did not come off: making both candidate roots unwritable on this volume ended in an ordinary install failure rather than the no-install-root branch, so that one is proven by its suite case alone and is recorded here as such rather than claimed as a real-surface run.
openQuestions: The reviewer's scope question — whether to narrow which fences are judged — was answered by the architect for this round and is implemented; nothing is left open there.
Unchanged: AC3's full line, AC4's daemon half and AC5's two-role form are production-check criteria, needing the worker image pin and the one `runtime.kubernetes.setup` line.

The reviewer's two structural majors are the body's `Fast-follow`: the guard's header duplicates its own subcommand table, `legion.ts`'s notice fan-out has no test on the delivered order, and `docs/kubernetes.md` still says the lock lives in `/legion/bun/state` when it is taken on the cache directory.
discoveredComplexity: The install half is not byte-identical for the next test round, as the reviewer warned: the backend, the lock's re-check, the log and the report path all moved, and the measured install now costs a second copy of the packages on the issue volume.
Every untrue sentence this round removed was one nothing asserted. The suite now holds each message the gate prints word for word, which is the only arrangement under which a message can be trusted.
